title: The workflow for bigger projects
caption: Break the project down first, keep one chat as the planner, and give each step a fresh chat that hands back one small result.

one-chat-is-too-small.title: One chat is too small
one-chat-is-too-small.script: Say you are planning your company's next summer party: 200 employees across five offices in Europe. Sometimes the project is bigger than one chat can hold: the whole summer party, with venues, catering, hotels and invitations. One chat would fill up, whatever window size you give it.

break-it-down-first.title: Break it down first
break-it-down-first.script: So you break it down first. Work backward from the outcome, what do I need to run this party, and then what do I need for that, until the next step is clear. You can ask the AI to help you with that.

one-planner.title: One planner
one-planner.script: Then one chat stays the planner. It keeps only the plan and the results, so it stays small and has room to spare.

a-fresh-chat-per-step.title: A fresh chat per step
a-fresh-chat-per-step.script: Each step goes to a fresh chat: venues, catering, invitations. That chat reads its files and fills up as much as it needs, hands the result back to the planner as one small card, and then you let it go. Next step, next fresh chat.

you-coordinate.title: You coordinate
you-coordinate.script: And you coordinate, like a project manager. This is what we call a workflow. Every chat has one job, so none of them runs long enough to blur its middle. That is the whole idea: the window is the AI's attention span, and managing it is your job. One honest caveat: the zones and numbers I gave you are rules of thumb and illustrations, and I have not tested every chat app, so watch your own chats and adjust. If you want a low-key place to start, take the next chat that drifts, ask it for a handoff, and open a new one with it. Thank you.
